answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work at registration: each new identity must compute a memory-hard puzzle whose output is cryptographically bound to its keypair, like shale that yields only under steady pressure. One machine can run many threads, but every attempt needs its own slab of RAM, so faking a whole reef of identities demands proportional memory rather than spare cycles. The work is non-transferable — one computation cannot mint two keys — so each ember of fake identity carries its own full hardware cost, and the cost cannot be amortized across identities.
